title: Evolution environment
description: One executable task, derived from a commit in this repository, with a verifier that was shown to fail against the pre-fix source and pass at HEAD. An environment that has not been shown that is in no set and scores nothing. `verification_at_fix` is the same verification taken in a worktree at the fix commit, `head` being the fix sha: whether the test discriminated the fix when it was written. Nothing that scores or assigns a set reads it, because an environment is posable only where its fix reverse-applies.

statement.description: What the agent is handed: the symptom, the number that was wrong, the screenshot. Never the fix. Null until authored, because it cannot be derived from a commit message that says what the fix was.

source.description: A fix_commit source also requires fix and parent; a decision_corpus source requires corpus. This schema language has no oneOf, so the per-kind requirement is enforced by Environments.validate/0 (shape_errors), with the function put/1 uses.

corpus.description: decision_corpus: the file under .agents/decisions/corpus/ the rows were drawn from.

selector.description: decision_corpus: how the rows were chosen — a population prefix and a k/n hash split.

subject.description: The commit subject. The answer sheet; not shown to a solver.

verifier.description: reverse_patch also requires app, files and source_paths; decision requires question, version, fingerprint, corpus, rows and rows_hash (Environments.Decision.validate_verifier/1).

fingerprint.description: decision: the question's fingerprint at that version. A different fingerprint is a different question, and the environment is then unavailable.

rows.description: decision: the corpus row ids asked. Their labels are the answers, so two environments in different sets may not share one.

rows_hash.description: decision: canonical hash of each row's id, label and evidence. Labels that moved after a model was scored make the environment unavailable, never re-verified.

files.description: Test files, relative to the app. Hidden from the agent solving the environment, which is why two environments in different sets may not share one.

source_paths.description: Repository-relative source paths the fix touched. These are what the verification reverse-applies.

set.description: One-way. A holdout that can be moved out of the holdout after a candidate fails on it is not a holdout.

verification_history.description: Append-only, newest last. An environment that verified in one month and stopped verifying in another is a fact about the test suite, visible only if both records survive.

state.description: rejected is a statement about the test; unavailable is a statement about our ability to ask. They are never interchangeable.

by.description: What the runner said it was. A claim, never checked — see by_attested.

by_from.description: Where the claim came from: an environment variable name, or the caller's option.

by_attested.description: Whether anything stands behind `by`. Read from `actor.attestation` since a design decision; false everywhere until something signs, and the field exists so that a gate cannot read the name without reading that.

actor.description: Who ran it, AWID-shaped. `attestation` is the only field a gate may read to decide whether anything stands behind the name.

discrimination.description: Did the test detect something, or did the tree simply stop compiling? Only `assertion` is evidence that the verifier discriminates. `decision`: the environment passed its labels and failed each answerer built to fail it (Environments.Decision).

head.description: The commit the verdict was taken at. Without it, `verified` goes on saying so after HEAD has moved past the commit it reverse-applies.

note.description: A fact about the verdict that is not the verdict — today, that the caller's working tree had uncommitted changes in the paths this verifier reads and the verdict is not about them.
